questions.question: Which of the following describes mechanical energy?
options: The sum of an object's kinetic and gravitational potential energy.
Only the kinetic energy of an object.
The difference between kinetic and potential energy.
The total thermal and kinetic energy.

questions.question: If an object is stationary on the ground, what is its mechanical energy?
options: Equal to its mass times gravity.
Maximum because it is at rest.

questions.question: What happens to the kinetic energy of an object if its velocity is doubled?
options: It increases by a factor of 4.

questions.question: Under what condition is the mechanical energy of a system conserved?
options: When there are no external non-conservative forces doing work on the system.
Always, regardless of the forces present.
Only when the object is falling downwards.
When friction is the only force doing work.

questions.question: Which equation correctly represents the conservation of mechanical energy?
If a system is NOT isolated (e.g. air resistance is present), what happens to the total mechanical energy?
options: It is not conserved; some mechanical energy is converted into other forms like heat.

questions.question: A 3 kg stone is dropped from rest from a height of 10 m. What is its initial kinetic energy?
When substituting values for an object dropped from a height $h$, what is the final potential energy just before it hits the ground?
A 1 kg object falls from 2 m. Which substitution correctly shows the initial state of the equation $(E_k + E_p)_i$?
